Information since June points to robust real activity and a tight labor market with inflation near 2% and expectations little changed. In New Keynesian frameworks with sticky prices and wages (Christiano, Eichenbaum, and Evans; Galí), such conditions warrant measured rate hikes to keep inflation near target without incurring excess real-side volatility. Anchored expectations (Woodford; Blanchard) justify gradualism, while credit-channel evidence (Bernanke and Mihov; Gertler) cautions that overly rapid tightening could amplify financial frictions, especially for smaller firms. With risks described as “roughly balanced” and policy still “accommodative,” the communication is positive and confidence-affirming, but not aggressively hawkish.
